data.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right under Part III of the Constitution of India today?
data.explanation: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the Right to Property from Part III; it is now a constitutional right under Article 300A. The other three are still Fundamental Rights (Articles 14–18, 23–24 and 32).
data.label: pyq-pattern

data.stem:
Consider the following statements about Article 19:
1. It guarantees six freedoms.
2. It is available to both citizens and foreigners.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
data.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Article 19 now lists six freedoms. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 19 freedoms are available only to citizens. So only 1 is correct.
data.label: pyq-pattern

data.stem: Free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 became a Fundamental Right through which amendment?
data.explanation: The 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21A. The 42nd added Fundamental Duties among other changes, the 44th removed the Right to Property, and the 73rd dealt with Panchayati Raj.
data.label: practice

data.stem: During a national emergency, the enforcement of which of the following articles cannot be suspended?
data.explanation: After the 44th Amendment, Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended. Article 19 is suspended automatically during an emergency declared on grounds of war or external aggression, and the right to move courts for other rights can be suspended.
data.label: pyq-pattern

data.stem: Which of the following writs is issued to an authority to stop it from acting beyond its jurisdiction while the matter is still pending?
data.explanation: Prohibition is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to stop proceedings beyond its jurisdiction. Mandamus commands a public duty, quo warranto questions a claim to public office, and habeas corpus secures release from unlawful detention.
data.label: practice
